comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: The test doesn't verify that `creatersbuild` (without a separator) is NOT matched, which would help catch the issue with the regex pattern being too permissive. Consider adding a negative test case like `npx creatersbuild` to ensure the pattern correctly requires a separator.
comments.label_reasoning: The comment points out a missing negative test case that would catch a regex being too permissive — a logic/correctness concern in the test coverage.

comments.author: shilman
comments.body: @copilot update this pull request to apply changes based on [this feedback](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/pull/33603#discussion_r2711080912)

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests adding a specific negative test case to verify the regex pattern doesn't match unintended strings.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: Consider adding test cases for edge cases and false positives, such as: commands where `@tanstack/start` appears in a URL or path (e.g., `npm install https://registry.com/@tanstack/start`), or commands with similar but not matching patterns. This would help verify the detection is specific enough.
comments.label_reasoning: The comment highlights missing edge case and false positive test coverage for a detection pattern, pointing to potential correctness issues.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests adding additional edge case and false positive test cases to improve test coverage.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body:
The regex pattern `create[\s\-]?rsbuild` makes the separator optional, which means it would also match `creatersbuild` (with no separator). This is likely unintended. Consider using `create[\s\-]rsbuild` (without the `?`) to require either a space or dash separator.
```suggestion
      const rsbuildMatch = ancestor.command?.match(/(?:^|\s)create[\s\-]rsbuild/i);
```
comments.label_reasoning: The regex pattern is too permissive due to `?` making the separator optional, causing unintended matches like `creatersbuild`. This is a logic error in the pattern.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Identifies a bug where the regex is too permissive and provides a concrete code suggestion to fix it.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.label_reasoning: Using `.includes('@tanstack/start')` is overly broad and can produce false positives when the string appears in URLs, paths, or comments. This is a logic error in the detection approach.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags a potential false positive issue with the string matching approach and provides a concrete code suggestion using a more specific regex pattern.
